Projects / Enterprise Equipment Loan and Asset Lifecycle Management

01 / Executive overview

From informal equipment lending to a governed asset lifecycle.

The organization issued equipment to clients across service locations without consistent visibility into asset holders, return dates or reliable equipment availability. Staff depended on manual checks and follow-up, making reassignment and overdue recovery difficult.

I led discovery, business analysis, solution architecture, implementation and delivery of a centralized Salesforce application. Guided loan registration, synchronized asset status, scheduled reminders and escalations, return inspections and automated eligibility controls established a more accountable equipment lifecycle.

Engagement at a glance

Technology: Screen Flows, Record-Triggered Flows, Schedule-Triggered Flows, Formula fields, Static Resources, Validation Rules, Email, Dashboards

02 / Problem and opportunity

Addressing blind spots across the lending process.

Inventory uncertainty

No reliable organization-wide view of which equipment was available, held by clients or under repair.

Reactive return follow-up

Manual reminders and inconsistent documentation obscured upcoming and overdue returns.

Policy enforcement gaps

Limited repeat-borrowing controls and fragmented oversight of recurring overdue behaviour.

03 / Business process transformation

As-Is and To-Be processes.

The To-Be diagram separates manual physical/IT inspection from Salesforce automation. An Asset is marked Returned by a user only after inspection has passed; then the Record-Triggered Flow updates the associated records. Repairing Assets remain unavailable until cleared.

04 / Technical solution design

A connected Salesforce architecture for lending, accountability and availability.

Implementation note: Supplementary Services is the loan-transaction record shown in the Salesforce schema. Inspection is conducted manually before a user marks a loan Returned; the record-triggered Flow then synchronizes loan and Asset records. The client borrowing ban activates automatically after more than 14 days overdue.

Formula-driven Asset Availability Status

The Asset formula field Asset_Availability_Status__c uses IMAGE() and Static Resources to display the current Asset Status as a coloured square in the Asset List View.

Available/colour_green
Loaned/colour_yellow
Overdue/colour_red
Out of Service (Repair)/bright_blue_colour
Retired/black_color

05 / Lifecycle controls

Automation, inspection and lending eligibility.

Scheduled follow-up

A daily Schedule-Triggered Flow evaluates Supplementary Services records: upcoming due loans receive client and internal reminders; initial overdue records trigger status updates, emails and manager-facing notifications; extended overdue loans receive further notices.

Return and inspection

Intake-bay physical inspection precedes IT technical checks. When cleared, a user marks the loan Returned; the Record-Triggered Flow synchronizes the loan and Asset. Equipment requiring repair is marked Out of Service (Repair) until ready for use.

Automated loan ban

When a loan is overdue by more than 14 days, automation sets Equipment Loan Ban to Active on the client Account. A filtered Client lookup and validation rule prevent further loan creation while the ban is active.

SMS notifications were considered as a future enhancement, not a delivered feature. The exact implementation path for ban activation was confirmed by the project owner but has not been demonstrated in the supplied Flow canvases.
